subject: zoology
question_text: What is metagenesis? Animals belonging to which phylum exhibit metagenesis?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.53, VSAQ 90). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What metagenesis is
steps.why: Each phase is named by the kind of reproduction it carries out, so the definition is complete only when both the asexual and the sexual generation are stated.
common_mistakes: Writing only 'alternation of generations'. Say which phase is asexual and which is sexual.
Calling it metamorphosis. Metamorphosis is a change of form within one animal; metagenesis is an alternation of two generations.
steps.memory_tip: Polyp buds, medusa makes gametes — the two phases follow each other.
steps.margin_note: One sentence of definition, then name the two phases. Three lines.
lines: Metagenesis is the alternation of an asexual
phase and a sexual phase in the life cycle of
The asexual polyp produces medusae by budding.
The sexual medusa produces the gametes.

steps.label: The phylum
steps.why: Only an animal that has two body forms can alternate them, and the polyp and the medusa are the two body forms of a cnidarian.
common_mistakes: Naming Porifera. Sponges have no medusa, so they show no metagenesis.
Leaving out the example. One named animal is expected.
steps.memory_tip: Two body forms, so two generations: only Cnidaria has both a polyp and a medusa.
steps.margin_note: Name the phylum and give one example. Keep it to three lines.
lines: Animals of the phylum Cnidaria show
Example: Obelia. Its fixed polyp colony buds
off free-swimming medusae, and the medusae

insider_note: The mark for the phylum is lost more often than the mark for the definition — write the word Cnidaria plainly, and add Obelia beside it.
